Subject: Acme RAG eval — reranker choice & retrieval settings (post-call recap)

Hi Sam / Priya —

Thanks again for the call earlier — good to align on the baseline evaluation and the primary concerns you flagged (precision for customer-support KB, hallucination floor for compliance content, and latency goal sub-300ms p95). Quick recap + proposed next steps so we can keep momentum for the POC: 

Summary from today:
- Scope: RAG assistant for Support KB (50k docs, mix of short articles + long policy pages) + internal compliance doc set (sensitive).
- Primary goals: improve grounding (precision) on support queries, avoid hallucination on policy answers, and keep end-to-end latency within your SLA.
- Current infra: Acme evaluating Pinecone + open-source re-ranker; prefer to avoid heavy cross-attention rerankers that add >100ms.

Immediate recommendations / next steps:
1) Retriever: dense with FAISS/HNSW, shard by doc type (support vs policy) — propose k=50 for recall sweep, then tune to k=8-12 for production. See attached retriever-config-proposal.yaml.
2) Reranker: recommend using a lightweight cross-encoder re-ranker for final top-8 reordering — models we recommend: redwood/mini-cross-bert-3 (fast, ~35ms on our infra) or redwood/cross-encoder-xxl for precision-sensitive queries in policy flows. Start with mini-cross for support KB, run a targeted eval on policy docs with cross-encoder-xxl.
3) Generator model: for POC, try 1) redwood-7b-q4f and 2) redwood-13b-int8 (compare quality vs latency).
4) Evals: we prepared a prompt set and suggested acceptance thresholds (precision@1 >= 90% for support, grounding score >= 95% for policy). Prompt set attached: acme_eval_prompt_set_v1.csv.
5) Benchmarks / Links: shared Redwood benchmark run (redwood-bench-202704.pdf) and the Drive folder with detailed evals.

Action items:
- Acme: confirm whether Neal at VectorDB should be included for retrieval tuning and provide a sample export of 200 representative support queries (Priya to share).
- Redwood (Marissa): run a mini-eval comparing the two reranker options against your sample queries (deliverable: ranking precision report + latency tradeoffs). Target deliverable by Fri 05/28.
- Redwood (Rishi): check model licensing / quantization options for cross-encoder-xxl and confirm expected GPU cost at POC scale.

Attachments: acme_eval_prompt_set_v1.csv, retriever-config-proposal.yaml, redwood-bench-202704.pdf

Thanks — I’ll kick off the eval runs once we have the sample queries.

Best,
Marissa

Thanks Marissa — this is great, appreciate the clear plan. A few quick clarifying q's before we finalize the sample export: 

1) On the reranker: how much precision uplift are you seeing empirically between the mini-cross and the xxl cross-encoder on policy-style (long-doc) queries? Ballpark numbers are fine for planning.
2) Latency: if we run mini-cross as the default and only use xxl for policy queries, can you estimate end-to-end p95 for a support query (FAISS k=12 -> mini-cross top8 -> generator redwood-7b-q4f)?
3) For the prompt set, do you recommend synthetic negatives (hard negatives) as part of retrieval eval, or should we start with human-labeled negatives?

Priya — we can share the 200 queries by EOD tomorrow. Neal — included you to confirm whether VectorDB can produce the export in the format Marissa requested (doc_id, chunk_id, text, metadata).

Sam

Sam — quick answers inline: 

1) Precision uplift: from our internal benchmarks on similar long-policy corpora, mini-cross vs no-rerank gives +10-14% precision@1; cross-encoder-xxl vs mini-cross shows an additional +4-6% precision@1 on long, dense-policy queries (but at ~3x latency). The delta is largest when the docs are long and contain overlapping sections; for short support articles the difference is smaller (~1-2%).

2) Latency estimate (p95, optimized infra): FAISS recall k=12 (10ms) -> mini-cross re-rank top8 (~35ms) -> generator redwood-7b-q4f (~160ms token generation p95 for short answers) + networking/overhead (~20-30ms) => ~230-250ms p95. If we swap to cross-encoder-xxl for the rerank step add ~80-120ms depending on batch and GPU type. These are estimates — we’ll report actual numbers after the mini-eval.

3) Hard negatives: recommend a mix. Start with human-labeled negatives for the first 50 queries to calibrate your evaluation set, then synthesize hard negatives from similar queries to stress test the retriever. We included a column in acme_eval_prompt_set_v1.csv to accept both types.

Next steps from our side: we’ll queue two mini-eval runs (mini-cross vs xxl on your sample) and push preliminary ranking precision + latency results by Fri 05/28. Rishi, I flagged licensing questions in our internal tracker — can you confirm the expected incremental cost for running cross-encoder-xxl in the POC?

Thanks — Marissa

I’ll post a short breakdown to the HubSpot deal and link it in the Drive folder by EOD.

Also tagging Dev for any security/residency flags since you mentioned policy docs may be sensitive. Dev — do you see any red flags for running the mini-eval on a Redwood-hosted POC environment?

-Rishi
